# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC’s phase sequence into **three levels of tasks that can be committed and verified
> independently**.
>
> RFC-039’s main text is the sole authority on phase order and acceptance gates; this document only
> breaks the work down to an executable granularity and records conflicts whose resolution is still
> pending.

## Purpose and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the phase sequence in RFC-039                     |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase that can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                 |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established: throughout this document’s history, the three
headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` have had zero matches (verifiable with
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no
repository-wide references to them. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that phase was decomposed into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s numbering aligns
with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered here**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and acceptance-criterion
bindings.

**Not covered here**: the design rationale for the tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the justification for
phase order (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered level-2/level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**owning phase**” (the P phase to which it truly belongs, which may
differ from the containing section) and “**blocks the mainline**.” `Registered, awaiting scheduling`
is no longer the default state; an unmarked item is considered **not schedulable**. Numbering must
be **unique across the entire document** (tasks on other tracks use their track number, such as
`029g.x`, and must not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable)—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not write
the fix, the criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a
dashboard, not a process log. **Do not write decision labels or restate conclusions**: “user
decision A/B/C,” “Plan A,” “Option A,” and “the final implementation is…” must not enter this table.
The dashboard answers only “complete or not”; consult the commit message and RFC-039’s decision
register for decisions and outcomes.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after push**: a closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push completes. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md), “Take the commit number
after push”). The closure commit itself has no short hash—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: the level-1/2/3 counts under `Purpose and Scope` contain
only current values; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Resolution                                                                                                                                                    |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC defines P5 (checker decomposition) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform the decomposition; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one `annotations.rs` entry, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                   | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                        |
| G2  | **The ownership of the three `include!` changes is unspecified, and none has been implemented**. RFC lists them under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; `06` also lists them under S7. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC and `06` have been synchronized to point here |
| G3  | **Three competing lists of CI scripts coexist**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` separately lists 4 checks with entirely different names; `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified list (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents must refer to this table                      |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life or death of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` argues for deletion                                                                                                                                                                                     | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision record C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                                         |
| G5  | **Conflict in the L2 goal statement**: RFC and this directory’s index previously said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | This has converged on a **declarative precedence table + unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3                   |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent / do not fill endlessly / do not
patch when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, reviving tests in P1 would already involve adding `mod` declarations
to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Solution)

Source: [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3, vulnerability-fix half + **2026-10-07
Silent-Discard-Point Audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, user decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a subsequent
> phase discovers a defect under which “the old behavior does not constitute success”—**A silent
> failure / B silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and uncontrolled resources** (crash, stack
> exhaustion, silently returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed in passing during the
> refactor**, but all four requirements must be met: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must
> exist first and must actually be red); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of
> programs that “previously compiled successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures,
> and their existing diagnostic codes / prose / exit codes must not be removed or changed); ③
> register it in the same commit (this row identifies the error class + that phase’s revision note +
> the PR required-block “Error Type” line); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually
> review the diff. **D user-visible semantics / E external contract table / F RFC-level design
> changes must still be decided first. See
> [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria and
> A–F allowlist; the approach of “default to a super-refactor and register it afterward” is not
> adopted** (rationale in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be distinguished from
> regressions, and this conflicts with both “no C5′” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

**Acceptance**: vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn
them red again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow C2/C3 and the 9.2 gates in P9. **Risk**: the new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus-differential baseline
and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Emergency stopgap path**: P3 does not need to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**; the
> remainder of P2 (2.1 IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping correctness vulnerabilities (`Sorted(3)`
> passing silently) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3
> (panic-to-diagnostic conversion) has no prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint.** It is distinct from P10 S5 “lower the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust-style
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order would mean redoing the same deletions
and baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| 029g Deletion Surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by Which Phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and grammar branches                                        | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexical convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                                     |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→true `mod` and checker decomposition are **pure moves**; the `pub` branches will be moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                                      |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slim down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `semantic_tokens` `Public` modifier                                 | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `is_pub`-ignoring binding in `ir_gen`                               | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (SSA-ify `ir_gen.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase modifies these directly, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires no differences in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-drive tests under `tests/` are excepted, as specified in P6’s hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: 029g deletes the dead `env.exports` table (populated by the producer with
zero repository-wide consumers) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4’s 4.3 obligation
ledger loses one “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first receive a red criterion
   before code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced
   top-level binding in Lib/Script roles newly reports W1001 (previously `pub` items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting `exempt_pub` cases and `is_pub` fixtures from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs`, equivalent new cases must replace them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (a new parse error + a new W1001) ⇒
   update the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero differences, and any non-zero difference
   requires an explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with 3.4 at the file level (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must
be serialized and must not run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g
track does not depend on 3.4; the implementer decides which to do first based on the context at
hand.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: the adoption of this section (P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint rows) and RFC-039’s D56 were included together in `97071c81b` when the
> parallel-stream cleanup swept the workspace—the commit message records “3.4 supplemental
> registration + D57/D58 decision archival” and does not mention this track. History is not
> rewritten; following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation
> note), it is registered in place as a retrospective bisection anchor.

|                                                  | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with **named arguments** loses the formal-parameter name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closeout): calling a cross-unit method (injected through the registry) with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional-argument calls to the same method work normally, and named-argument calls within a single file work normally. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, whereas `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (the old behavior was not success: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by runtime failure or a silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—obtain the declared formal-parameter names from the unique cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` using the definition-unit qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (the candidate ↔ mixed-IR-name ↔ formal-parameter-name vectors are in the same order, with the same source as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table instead of using two bare-name segments. These two locations fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate-injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments on alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “the same input produces multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**; this is not a fix of the original bug. Criterion = the same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is permitted for a method key; removing ascending-order merge produces two results). **Criterion (red first, then green)**: 2 driver-level cases in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import single candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name, 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; file header marked as a history gate); unit tests in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (an empty-name-table guard for `method_param_info` ⇒ None, and a positive control returns the non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the determinism criterion above). Project-level fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with the alias-surface retirement); the corpus differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` is now 404 lines: **relative to direct parent `ac810e97`, 405→404** (an intermediate state once contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 base fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). The line-count change is an unavoidable result of fixtures entering/leaving (`corpus_probe` regeneration is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline), **not coverage loss**. **Known Gaps (named individually; old behavior = silent ignore or silent discard; D60② should have been reported, Class A)**: closure value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / builtin-container constructors other than `len` named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these have been corrected against P0’s measured baseline**: ① **static-function shapes** (both same-unit and cross-unit, declaration and binding forms) are **entirely unavailable today**—same-unit `check` reports E3006, cross-unit declaration-form `run` reports E6007, and cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code, so this is unrelated to named arguments and is not “named arguments silently discarded”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), because the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table, which is likewise unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 Class A fixed in passing: the old E6007/E1014 behavior was not success, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These previously produced, respectively, runtime E6007 with silently dropped arguments and check-time `E1014 (available: )` false rejection; all now bind by declared formal-parameter name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file’s header history gate). One identity-surface residual remains after the other was closed: this unit’s own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the local declaration) **has been closed with 4.9.10-S2a’s import-surface work** (the project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is fully green); the remaining case is function-body-level / cross-scope imports merged globally per unit (a shared import table)—that shape does not work to begin with (an existing defect: `check` passes, `run` reports E6006), was not introduced by this batch, and remains unfixed. **Deleted in this round (relative to the first six rounds of 4.9.9)**: candidate-provider priority, candidate-signature comparison, owner/compatibility inference, the `frontend::module::import_face` shared-provider table, the IR-side “no name table ⇒ E1014” fallback, and the **E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution**—the latter rejects mixed/alias-only shapes that ran on the parent commit (Class D), and the 2026-11-26 decision withdrew it; this round introduces no new ambiguity judgment. **Visible changes**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (**bare-name imports**, including two same-named overload candidates) change from E1014 with an empty table to binding by name (measured 6.0 / 30); ② all other shapes return to pre-4.9.9 behavior (named arguments silently ignored or discarded; see “Known Gaps”); ③ single method binding no longer varies with HashMap iteration order for the same input (Class C). **Status**: completed 2026-11-26 (including the narrowing round and a passing review). | 4.9.7         | Criteria are in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` and `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs` (the latter added with 4.9.10-S2b), and `src/frontend/module/registry.rs`; |                                                  | 4.9.10 Cross-unit method identity is undefined (registered 2026-11-25, confirmed as a structural issue during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not include module qualification, so when same-named types exist across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`driver::arms::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-parameter-name / candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each guess the provider by name, and a change to any one location merely moves the “silent wrong value” elsewhere. **Root solution**: upgrade type identity to a **module-qualified identity** (`{module}.{Type}`), and change the method-candidate key accordingly to `{module}.{Type}.{method}`; one resolver produces the identity and the three locations only read it. This requires changing the shape of the `overload_resolutions` key and mixed-IR names; D59 **Class D** (requires a decision). **Disposition in this round (based on the two narrowing rounds of 4.9.9)**: 4.9.9 **introduces no new rejection**—the earlier Class D rejection list (named arguments always E1014 / conflicting shapes with positional arguments always E1107 / E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution) is deleted along with the mechanism and all entries are void; the parent commit’s runnable mixed / alias-only / conflicting **import shapes and positional arguments** are restored to working order. **Residual surface (after this round closes)**: ① function-body-level / cross-scope imports merged globally per unit (a shared import table), and that shape does not work to begin with (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006); ② shapes in which named arguments are still silently ignored or discarded (D60② Class A): **static-function shapes** (same-unit `check` E3006; cross-unit declaration-form `run` E6007; cross-unit binding-form `run` E6006—positional and named arguments produce the same code and are unrelated to named arguments), **RFC-004 cross-unit** (positional arguments likewise report E6006), **closure value binding**, **block-body function declaration**, and **builtin containers other than `len`** (`size` and similar shapes: named arguments are ignored, `length` is 0, and runtime reports E6005; the `len` shape works normally). **Three items closed with this round**: ① method-candidate / method keys changed to module-qualified `{module}.{Type}.{method}` (L0’s `DefPath` dual representation + S2a’s table key and single-point resolution; the three consumers named at registration—`visible_method_overloads`, formal-parameter-name reverse lookup `method_param_info`, and `method_dispatch_name`—have all been deleted); ② this unit’s own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist); ③ alias import / namespace arm / inferred-receiver named arguments (three shapes turn green; see the corresponding section of 4.9.9). **L3 type-identity residuals (migration surface, unfixed; already red at L0 and not a regression from this round)**: ① the type name itself is still not module-qualified—the static type name in `MonoType` is the **defining-side bare name**, so same-named types across units still cannot be distinguished at the type layer and can only be worked around through the import surface + binding identity; ② `VarInfo::type_identity` covers only **local binding** registration locations (written annotation / constructor write path); **formal parameters, pattern bindings, closure formal parameters, and `for` variables** are not registered—at those locations, the receiver can still be resolved only by static type name (`set_type_identity` has only one call site across the repository). **Status**: closed (2026-11-29). L0 / S1 / S2a / S2b and L3 (type-representation-layer identity, D64) are all implemented—single identity encoding (`types/identity.rs` is the sole home of `DefPath`/`DefId`/`DefKind`/`TypePath`/`Nominal`; `module::symbol` has zero re-exports; `from_def_path` enforces an empty owner, zero disambiguation, and legal bare names); five nominal surfaces carry `Nominal`; `rebind_nominal_refs`/`qualify_deferred_method`/`import_type_rebinds` are fully removed; `env.types` / sum types / record models / generics / lower’s two tables are queryable by identity (`TypeEnvironment::add_type` writes “identity → first written name” and “written name → identity” in the same commit, with a single writer); display and hashing still use bare names (`Debug`/`Display`/`type_name`/`to_type_id`/vtable keys have zero diff). |                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point as “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving the impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer uses `&mut self` to implicitly write to the error channel; the diagnostic set is returned to the caller, and the sole write point is the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Reason for not leaving the impl**: the only field in this family is `self.env` (a purely technical surface, so leaving the impl is possible), but changing “both the entry point and the traversal” to free functions would also move these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test site, and it would create a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection) → refinement”—contrary to the coupling-reduction intent of this step | 5.2.1         | —                                                                                                                                                 |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever migrated with the annotation family, **then** `checker.rs` must add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the existing import remains unchanged; 5.3 did
not migrate it as measured, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of merely 200–400 lines—this increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> one set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **only input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> decision** (identical after normalizing both sides; does not bind type variables); evidence is the
> **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (holding for closed, open,
> and recursive terms); Σ constructor points **reuse** the same evidence interface rather than
> establishing another one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that subphase names
> have been checked off.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 decision → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, while d leans types/solver→sema); C.2 may run
> in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D implementation waits
> for confirmation of the B design package; it depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and
> may depend on 6.9.3’s typed exit. **P7 gate = A/B/C exits; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 decision (A decided on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation layer’s `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`.
> **The decision is changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1 second field and C-2 reconstruction from IR both
> break the single representation/evaluator, C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing causes the
> recursive chain to hit `max_depth` and E3005; T-a condition on instance depth / T-b bounded
> firing + fallback to the original at the boundary / T-c termination layer or change the
> specification). **Measure first, then decide; before measurement, “A can now be implemented” must
> not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8;
> C3 implementation is a separate task and does not claim complete I4.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “decision points first use unification; after unification fails, definitional equality may be
> used, but the partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (have no unbound
> variables); what are the snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; and do unify and defeq share
> one budget or each have their own. **Responsibility boundary**: unify continues to handle
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only decides equivalence and does not take over subtyping, and
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; 6.9.3c’s wiring contract wasted two rounds
> because it assumed `can_assign` was the decision point, and `AssignmentChecker` has zero
> production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero corpus/IR
> snapshot drift or a per-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected integration tests;
> ③ error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point/code table is changed); ④ classification
> under D59 and red first, then green for behavioral changes. **Wiring tasks additionally require**:
> production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many paths, which is reachable);
> using unit-test reachability as a substitute for user reachability is prohibited; rollback and
> budget must have measured figures. **Residual disposition**: #537 (Class D, proof-function
> formal-parameter refinement is silently discarded; do not fix before a decision, and 6.9.4/6.9.5
> must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; Class C boundary, if unclosed then 6.9.4
> covers only module-local code), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 closed
> 2026-11-14: orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 +
> E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—three sites moved forward and back
> together on 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` /
> `drop_erased_call_args` through the single-point `rewritten_call_target` cover `Call`/`TailCall`,
> and init sections and function bodies share one site-rewriting source; red→green + three
> mutations), #542 (isolated shared layer; **implemented (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two
> entry-point connections + C2c temporary workaround removal; red→green, 402/402, function-table
> attribution and deviations), #552 (imported multi-parameter predicate proof execution; in the
> 6.9.5 neighborhood, separate case). **Ownership awaiting decision**: the four open-constraint
> tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality
> bridge; decide whether they remain in 6.9.4’s outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function
> surface.

> **Non-claims / boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim complete Π/Σ; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does not
> fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is not in
> this item; witness erasure ≠ runtime-check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 cover only
> shapes that do not depend on proof-function formal-parameter refinement; if #539 is not fixed,
> 6.9.4 covers only module-local code; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 is implemented (2026-11-19);
> 2.1.4’s inner-isolation red state was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten according
> to slot identity in the 2.1.4 closeout) ⇒ **all prerequisites for turning `verify` into a gate
> have been removed**.

**Hard acceptance** (**2026-10-27 revision, following 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly exercise the changed
code, such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the
change, but each modification must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must
not be deleted and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral fix**
batch (new diagnostic codes + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion,
and is handled as a separate round with a separate decision.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criterion (2026-10-26 decision ②) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a zero-difference requirement to all of `tests/`; the
> revised criterion **changes only direct-drive test files from “zero difference” to “modifiable but
> file / line count / reason must be registered”**. The **corpus layer** (`tests/yaoxiang`),
> **baseline layer** (`tests/baselines`), and **standard library** (`src/std/`) retain their
> zero-difference requirements. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs`
> changed, by **3 lines** (2 `assert_format_eq` occurrences of `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), with
> the reason = the assertion’s expected type name must track the changed spelling; no tests were
> deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6 6.1 Name Normalization Closeout.”

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority; missing a consumer will **silently change
associativity** (no error, only a different parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; any new operator must enter both the table
and the cross-validation test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on `08`’s D0/D2**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code references `sema` in reverse, `check-boundary.py` will block it.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 emergency-stoppage path (user decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The remainder of P2 (2.1
> IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can proceed
> in parallel with P3. Stopping correctness vulnerabilities must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must **be written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to be frozen into the phase table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g’s (#399) deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, checker layout, and IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker decomposition modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **P7’s gate = the phase A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface, but must not establish parallel ledgers; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume an undecided defeq/quantifier interface |
| P7/P8 → P9                | 9.5’s snapshot baseline and 9.3’s `pub(crate)` leak count take their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                             |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three criterion layers are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly says S5 “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5’s snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same file batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serialized).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move batch that precedes P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm
must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor is required”; only
  D0–D4’s review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three competing lists that constituted
  original gap G3 prevented closure. This table merges them, with 10 active scripts each assigned to
  one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), making report-only status and hardening
  timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 adopts RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to be done after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactor means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar,
  checker layout, and IR; this is the same lesson as adopting `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC status
  correction into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker decomposition would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero consumer changes” as the hard acceptance criterion**—the decomposition must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says that “fixed defects
  must not be rolled back” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix’s commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as a retrospective bisection anchor.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into the exclusive commits
  7b.1a / 7b.1b under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renamed references; missing one **silently
  changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; opcode reclamation for D32/D34 was merged into 7e.1, while the
  deletion action landed under P10 S6.1 (6753bbe).
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned a “separate issue”**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was adopted into 7e.3; `2315` was rechecked on 2026-11-28 and found to be
  an audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no
  throw/try/catch), 7e.2 was cancelled, and the exception residue was deleted under P10 S6.1
  (6753bbe).
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into P10
  S6.2’s generation-time gate task and implemented (a2e570c).

## Conflict Register: All Resolved

> **The original “Conflict Register” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Register](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** No pending items remain in this document. The correspondence is:

| Original ID | Issue                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| C1          | Revive `precedence_inline.rs` in P1 or delete it in P8                              | **Revive it** (P1’s prerequisite is that revival provides real assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                              |
| C2          | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs table-driven implementation                          | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + cross-validation of two `BinOp` implementations from the same source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3          | Conflict between C6’s category definition and S1’s classification                   | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); C6’s definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                   |
| C4          | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` allowlist                                        | **No allowlist**; the difference set must be empty. If it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                          |
| C5          | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 already lists it as a mandatory verification item**; confirm line by line during implementation                                                                               |
| C6          | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                                 | **Merge the wasm-path vulnerability fix into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                        |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assign to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                                     |
| C8          | Fix `upvalue_count` and bump the `.42` version number                               | **Fix + bump `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                                      |
